options.name: Memory Lab
options.rationale: Makes representations, slices, and allocation tradeoffs visible before introducing benchmark claims.

visualDirection.thesis: Inspect the bytes, then reason about the cost.
visualDirection.layout: dark technical workbench with a persistent byte inspector and guided experiment cards
visualDirection.type: system sans for prose with a legible monospace specimen layer
visualDirection.interaction: editable inputs update byte views and cost annotations with explicit reset controls
visualDirection.tradeoff: denser than a conventional article, but strongest for causal performance reasoning

options.name: Search Map
options.rationale: Organizes APIs around the learner's task and makes choosing an operation feel like navigating a map.

visualDirection.thesis: Choose a path from intent to operation.
visualDirection.layout: bright editorial map with branching task paths and compact comparison panels
visualDirection.type: humanist serif headings with neutral sans body copy
visualDirection.interaction: a task chooser reveals matching APIs, constraints, and worked examples
visualDirection.tradeoff: highly approachable, but less suited to close inspection of memory behavior

options.name: Benchmark Dossier
options.rationale: Teaches skepticism by treating every speed statement as a claim with workload and environment evidence.

visualDirection.thesis: A number is not a conclusion without its workload.
visualDirection.layout: paper-like evidence dossier with claim cards, annotated charts, and confidence stamps
visualDirection.type: editorial slab headings with tabular numerals and restrained body text
visualDirection.interaction: learners vary workload assumptions and see which conclusions remain supported
visualDirection.tradeoff: excellent for benchmark literacy, but gives less space to API exploration
